reaction: Back to a hill on 19 August. Last time I could not picture the safe room. I want to try again, slowly this time, and find out what deeper means.
Last time Steady ate a day while I read. I am choosing Slow straight away.
The wide view is much easier than my phone was. The cellar is a little room with three jars and someone in it. I will mark stone straight down below it, going deeper on purpose.
The same sentence as last time: Dig deeper, or shut doors on every open route. This time there is a More. I want to see if it says how deep.

Oh. There it is: riders search 9 passage steps from each opening, count steps, not depth. That is the depth I could not find last time; it was inside More. I reread it twice. So I need a winding passage longer than nine steps, and the beds at the far end. That is a puzzle I can actually picture.
One more square straight down, then I will turn the passage sideways so it winds.

Just after a minute. I resumed, chose Slow at nine seconds, and chalked a passage down from the cellar and then sideways. The More section told me the rule I missed last time: nine passage steps. Now the reading says three places are beyond riders reach. That is the first time this hill has said anything is safe. I feel clever, a little. Nobody has dug any of it yet.
One more square at the far end so more of the room is past nine steps.
And one more. Six safe now; I want room for six people.
Now I will let people choose to dig. Slow speed.
A day passed in thirty seconds even on Slow. Meryem is digging at my chalk now. Kian still needs to care for his sister Ada, which is a small human line I like. I will watch the room grow.
Meryem broke through again, coughing dust. Storage is asking already, same as last time. I want to see how far the digging got.

I can see my whole plan this time: a row of little pickaxe squares, and the last three are shaded grey. I am guessing grey means past the riders. One square under the cellar is already open. This is so much clearer than my phone last time.
The jars want a store. Let me see what furnish offers.
The right end of the cellar is reachable by riders anyway, so jars can go there and the safe end stays for beds.
The store took one tap and answered plainly. Now the jars need carrying down. I will wait and watch.
Water dry again, like last time. It says tap here for water, so I will. The repeated news lines are piling up, Repeated 4 times.

Knowing the nine-step rule turned this from guessing into a little puzzle I can see. Water is just something people fetch on their own, so I do not have to manage it. Meryem is my only digger, and I am waiting on her.
I want to see who the six people are; last time I only met Meryem.
Tamar of the Wall is a lovely name. Who is she?
She teaches Kian, who is not her child. I like that. More activity and words sounds like what I want.
Her words are generic: This helps me get closer to what I want. I was hoping for something about Kian. She needs rest, so I will not invite her out.
A road story! That is the unusual reply. Yes please.
Pending until a quiet moment. Time is paused while I read, so I will close this and let the day run.
Oops, Close only took me back to the village list and time stayed paused for 25 seconds. Closing again.

Oh, Kian answered! The Very Small King lets nobody in who is taller than the owner. Ada invented that one. That is exactly the kind of small line I came for, and it is about a door, which is funny for a shelter game. Also: digging stopped where daylight does not reach. That may be why my room never grew last time. I need a lamp.
A lamp in the little square under the cellar, right beside where my passage starts.
The lamp is hanging. Now let us see if Meryem keeps going.
This is the requested phone check, separate from how I want to play. I know this hill from my phone last time.

On the phone picture the cellar is pushed off to the right edge behind the zoom buttons and the reading covers the lower half; the water text is cut mid-sentence above the tools. I could not have seen my passage there. Back to the wide screen.

The passage is growing: two squares in the lower row are open now, and the jars moved into the store end of the cellar. The view has scrolled down on its own. The little dots on the floor might be loose stone; I am guessing. Five chalk squares left, three of them grey.
The room is slowly getting dug and I understand why, but the news is now mostly Repeated 7 times, Repeated 8 times. Kian’s story is the only new voice, and it is drifting down the list.
I want to try Master Yusuf or Maryam, to see if someone else has a story.

Her son Yusuf stayed behind at the well settlement. Wait, there is a Master Yusuf here too; another Yusuf, I guess. A smooth leftover piece of material is such an odd little gift that I have to offer it.
Meryem has gone to harvest barley, so nobody is digging. I will wait to see what Maryam says about the material.

Maryam brought out a wooden ring and string: Some are impossible knots. I keep the mistakes too. I love that. My sister would want that puzzle. But it sits in the news list between Repeated 9 times lines, and I cannot pick up the ring or answer her. Is there a way to try the knot? I do not see one.
Going back to Maryam to see if the knot puzzle is something I can follow up.
Answered, and the offer is now greyed out. So the puzzle is a line, not a puzzle for me. A little disappointing, but she was specific. I will look at Master Yusuf.
An old map! Yes, I want to compare it.

Yusuf showed a crossed-out passage and admitted he kept people working past the agreed time. A mark must show others when they can stop me. That is a real confession, and I read it twice. Who is the injured worker? It says they decide how to respond, but I cannot see them. I want to know.
Maybe the Journal keeps these stories somewhere I can reread.
The Journal is the same list. Nothing about the injured worker. Back to the hill.
A family asked for room below and went on because there were no beds. That stung a little. I need to see how much is dug so I can put beds in.

No progress since the 25th; still two open squares in the lower row and five chalk squares waiting. The view jumped up again on its own, which is a bit disorienting. I am guessing the far wall is dark again, so I will hang a second lamp at the end of the open passage.
Second lamp is up. Waiting to see if anyone digs toward the grey squares.
Nobody mentions digging in the news. Who is doing what?
This list reads word for word like it did on the 26th: Yusuf still on the way to eat, Meryem still harvesting. Either they are stuck or the panel is stale. Checking Meryem.
The barley must be harvested before it is ruined. Fair enough, she has her own priorities. I will not pull her away. So my shelter waits for the harvest.

The people stories are the best part, Kian, Maryam and Yusuf each had one specific line. But each one was a single line, and the dig has stalled for the harvest. I am waiting, and the news is mostly Repeated eleven times.
Tariq has been sitting by the entrance for days. I have not met him.

Recognition guess at 608s: Tariq’s stepmother is Zehra, and his father is Yusuf at the well settlement. In Valley there was a Zehra who answered the call with the same sentence as everyone. Confidence low: only a shared name, nothing else connects them. My reaction: a small flicker, oh, maybe that Zehra, but I do not believe it strongly. It does explain Maryam’s son Yusuf, though: he is Tariq’s father, not Master Yusuf. Two Yusufs. That untangled itself nicely.
His own experiment. Yes.

Tariq is making a tiny boat and showed me a drawing of a failed sail. I will test it away from drinking water. Very sweet. But This experiment does not qualify him to build boats sounds like a rule talking, not a person. Every gift becomes one line and the button greys. I am collecting little postcards, which I like, but nothing comes back to me after.
Still the same two open squares as a week of game time ago, and my second lamp is hanging there. Someone is climbing down the shaft. I want to know why nobody digs.

Smoke on the southern hills, more than a field fire. My heart jumped. Nobody is safe yet; the far grey squares are not dug. It is real smoke, so I ring the bell, even though below ground is still reachable.
The bell is ringing. I am watching who comes down, tense.

Riders may be half a day away and Meryem and Tamar will come after they finish eating at the hearth. I almost laughed. It is the same I cannot do it now, after I finish this task line Halil said in Voice. I know people choose, but dinner before riders makes me anxious rather than respectful. And there is nowhere safe for them to go anyway.

Scouts only. Nobody hurt, but the report goes person by person: if the riders had attacked, she would have been caught. Everyone would have been caught. Kian’s reply to the bell was I am asleep. That is honestly a bit funny and also chilling. This is the clearest the stakes have ever felt, and it says they may return with more riders. Now I really want those grey squares dug.
The scout visit made the shelter matter. I understand exactly who would have died and why.
I want to ask Meryem to dig, maybe by inviting her to mark the route together.

I am very hungry, so I will eat first. That is a good, human reason, and the page clearly tells me her next choice is in 11 minutes. I will invite her to mark a route together; maybe that is the closest thing to asking her to dig.

Meryem showed which ground she saw herself and which lines came from older maps: I left those marks off the clean map. I need to put them back. That echoes her grandfather’s crossed-out passage, marks that show where the uncertainty is. I noticed the rhyme between them, and I liked noticing it. The scouts rode off; next time they may strike. Still nobody is digging.

Everyone is resting in the shade or sitting. Nobody has touched my chalk in ten game days, even after riders came, and I cannot tell why. Master Yusuf keeps discussing the marks; some stone may still be loose. Is that what blocks it? I am back where I was last visit: I know what I want, and the hill is not telling me what is in the way. I would stop here. I will keep going for the time I set aside.
I will use look on the next chalk square to see what it says about it.
Nine places beyond riders’ reach if dug. So the plan is right; it just is not being dug. People choose when to dig is all it says. I cannot find the reason.
Seventeen times now. Let me open this line in case it says more about loose stone.
Tapping Yusuf’s line just reopened the plan reading. No word about the loose stone.
Ten game days and nobody has dug my squares. I like the people, but the shelter has stopped and I cannot find the reason anywhere I look.
There is an I am confused choice this time. That is what I am. Selecting it locally; I will type nothing and press no Submit.
I'm confused is pressed; the note box looks empty. One last look at the hill before I go.

I am stopping on 7 September with the game menu open. This visit was much better than my last: the More section finally told me about the nine passage steps, I could see my plan on the wide screen, and the hill said nine places would be safe. Kian’s Very Small King, Maryam’s impossible knots, Tariq’s little boat and Yusuf’s crossed-out passage were each lovely. The scouts made the danger real. But after the 25th nobody dug another square, everyone rested, and I could not find out why. My wish to stop did not pass. I would not leave it running. I would return another evening if I knew what stops people digging a marked plan, because I want to see those six beds past the ninth step. I selected I am confused locally, typed nothing and pressed no Submit.
